text:
HSTU already supports sampled-softmax training: Meta’s public configuration uses 128 negatives, normalized embeddings and temperature 0.05. These are reference settings, not established Amazon optima. [Official configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin). Research supports investigating easy-negative saturation: sampled softmax emphasizes informative negatives, but excessively low temperatures let a few very hard examples dominate gradients. Strong sampled training margins therefore do not establish held-out ranking quality. [Sampled-softmax analysis, 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf).

For sampling correction, RecSys 2025’s “Correcting the LogQ Correction” identifies a subtle error: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its revised objective handles that distinction and introduces uncertainty-based weighting; blindly subtracting log sampling probability from every logit misses this issue. This addresses proposal-distribution bias, not false-negative labels. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331). A separate sequential-recommendation study finds sampling benefits depend on dataset popularity structure; popularity-based negatives can improve balance while reducing aggregate accuracy. [Study, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276).

Suggested experiment, rather than an established Electronics result: retain one HSTU per category; compare more uniform negatives, corrected sampled softmax, and a gradual mixture of uniform and moderately hard negatives selected by the same network. Exclude padding, target collisions and observed training positives; downweighting suspected false negatives remains a heuristic because unobserved preference is unknown. Earlier false-negative research confirms the issue, although its teacher-based procedure falls outside this experiment’s constraints. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116). Prioritize Electronics diagnostics, but select exclusively by the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10.
